Subject: Request: SLA exception for Falcon-XL-v2 beta rollout

Jonas / Redwood team,

We're planning to launch a pilot of Falcon-XL-v2 in a limited capacity next month (regional subset of users). ACME is excited to move quickly, but our procurement and security teams require a written commitment on uptime and latency guarantees as part of the pilot scope.

To be clear: this is a beta/preview deployment with an expectation of occasional degradations. Our security team is willing to accept an exception if Redwood documents the operational mitigations, escalation path, and a temporary SLA that reflects the preview status.

Key asks from our side:
- A short-term uptime commitment for the pilot window (two weeks) and an agreed fallback model if latency exceeds thresholds.
- A mechanism for credits or remediation if service is unavailable beyond agreed windows.
- A single point of contact and runbook for incident response during the pilot.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a temporary carveout SLA for the Falcon-XL-v2 preview, and if so, the suggested terms? Happy to take a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Sally Park
Senior Product Manager — AI Integrations
ACME Corp

Thanks — reading through the pilot scope. Below is a draft of the exception terms that we can present to ACME as a temporary addendum for the two-week pilot. I've kept the language concise so procurement can review quickly.

DRAFT — Beta/Preview SLA Addendum (2-week pilot)
- Effective period: 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-15 (pilot window).
- Scope: Applies only to requests routed to the Falcon-XL-v2 preview model for the ACME pilot, region: us-west-2.
- Uptime target: 95.0% availability (measured at 1-minute checks) during the pilot.
- Latency objective: median p95 latency <= 800ms for 95% of requests; not an SLA breach metric except where sustained for >30 minutes.
- Credits: For any daily uptime below 95.0%, ACME will receive a prorated service credit equal to 10% of daily billable usage for that day, capped at 50% of the pilot fees.
- Fallback: Automatic routing to Falcon-GA-v1 if p95 latency >1200ms for a continuous 15-minute window; customers notified via email and incident ticket.
- Exclusions: Maintenance windows with 72-hour notice; force majeure; customer-caused traffic spikes where traffic exceeds agreed pilot baseline by >3x.
- Operational obligations: Redwood to provide a dedicated on-call contact during pilot (PagerDuty + phone); incident runbook and postmortem within 72 hours of a P1.

Notes / questions:
- Karthik — can you confirm the automatic routing fallback and the 15-minute continuous window is implementable without additional infra changes?
- Jonas — if ACME wants a shorter credit latency trigger, procurement will push back. This is intentionally conservative.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Quick infra check and approval from my side.

Summary of technical constraints and confirmation:
- Automatic fallback: feasible. We already have routing policies that can pin to a GA model variant; routing policy change will be handled as a configuration update and does not require a code rollout.
- Detection window: 15-minute continuous p95 > 1200ms is implementable with existing metrics. We will create an automated trigger in the routing service and an incident will be opened in INF-4219 if triggered.
- Monitoring: We'll provide a shared dashboard and short-term retention for the pilot (30 days) for debugging.
- Latency caveat: For the first 48 hours of the pilot we expect higher variance as KV caches warm and quantization paths stabilize. Recommend we exclude the first 24 hours from credit calculation.

I'll attach a short performance brief with observed p95 numbers from our internal canary runs. If legal approves the draft above and ACME signs the addendum, infra can rollout the routing change 24 hours before pilot start.

—Karthik
